source: Holton, Mackridge & Philippaki-Warburton, Greek: An Essential Grammar, 2nd ed. (Routledge, 2016), upload 7635aa83 (PDF pp. 47-50 = §3.1-3.2). Copyrighted, no open license stated: rules are restated in our own words, examples limited to single words and short phrases. Continued from upload 86b689c6 (PDF pp. 56-60 = §3.48-3.51 start). Continued in upload 418329ba (PDF pp. 1-21 = rest of §3.51 to §3.57). Examples restated/shortened; rules in own words.

constituents.rule: A noun phrase is a noun alone or with modifiers; all declinable words in it agree with the noun in gender, number and case. It may also be headed by an adjective or pronoun, or be a clause introduced by neuter το.

patterns.pattern: quantifier + demonstrative + def. art + adj + noun

patterns.en: the fact that they lost the elections

functions.el: Θα του δώσουμε τα ρούχα του.
Θα του δώσουμε του Στέφανου τα ρούχα του.
functions.note: More often expressed with σε + acc: Θα δώσουμε στον Στέφανο τα ρούχα του.

functions.function: object of an everyday preposition (σε, από, με, για…)
functions.note: Some mostly learned prepositions take the genitive instead: λόγω της βροχής, εναντίον του, μεταξύ των χωρών.

functions.function: content/measure (same case as head, unlike English 'of')
functions.el: ένα κιλό πατάτες; τρία μπουκάλια κρασί
functions.en: a kilo of potatoes; three bottles of wine

predicate_rule: A predicate takes the case of the word it describes: nominative for the subject, accusative for the object.
stopped_at: Complete through §3.57 (end of Ch. 3). Next: Ch. 4 pronouns (see pronouns-holton.json).

agreement.rule: Every declinable modifier (article, determiner, adjective, numeral, quantifier) agrees with its noun in gender, number and case.

examples.el: Ο άλλος μικρός δρόμος είναι πιο δύσκολος.
examples.en: The other little road is more difficult.

examples.el: στη μέση της άλλης μικρής πλατείας
examples.en: in the middle of the other little square

multiple_nouns.rule: One modifier for several human nouns: masculine plural if any is masculine.
Non-human nouns: modifier usually agrees with the nearest noun.
Several modifiers may share one singular noun that stands for several entities.
multiple_nouns.el: ο Έλληνας και ο Τούρκος αντιπρόσωπος

case_uses.note: Only masculine -ος nouns show four distinct forms (singular).

uses.el: Η Μαρία έφυγε. / Φυλακίστηκε ο κλέφτης.
uses.en: Mary left. / The thief was imprisoned.
I consider him a friend of mine.

uses.el: Ο Γιάννης ήρθε από την Αθήνα.
Έτρεξα τρία χιλιόμετρα. / Κράτησε ένα χρόνο.
uses.en: I ran three kilometres. / It lasted a year.

examples: την Κυριακή το απόγευμα (on Sunday afternoon)

examples.en: a stick ten centimetres in length

uses.note: two alternative ways of saying the same thing

examples.en: I live two streets further down.

examples.el: Η αδελφή μου είναι ένα χρόνο μεγαλύτερη/πιο μεγάλη από μένα.
examples.en: My sister is one year older than me.

uses.use: location at / motion to (colloquial; place name without article)

examples.en: I'll be in Corinth. (cf. nom. η Κόρινθος)
Are you going to Ambelokipi? (cf. nom. οι Αμπελόκηποι)

uses.note: the word in square brackets is inserted in less colloquial usage

genitive.title: The use of the genitive
genitive.rule: A genitive noun phrase either is governed by a verb (most commonly as indirect object) or depends on a noun, where it is roughly the equivalent of English 's or 'of'.

governed_by_verb.rule: With a verb, a genitive weak pronoun (rarely a full noun phrase) is normally the indirect object. A noun-phrase indirect object is more usually expressed with σε + accusative (§8.2).

uses.use: person to whom something is given or said
person for whom the action is done
uses.en: I've got strawberries for you today.

uses.use: person from whom something is removed
uses.en: They took the shoes from him / They took his shoes.

examples.en: He dropped his handkerchief (lit. to/from him fell the handkerchief).
One of my teeth has broken (δόντι = subject) OR (S)he/it broke one of my teeth (δόντι = direct object).

uses.use: object of certain verbs with no direct object (αρέσω, πάω, φαίνομαι)

examples.el: Δεν μου αρέσει αυτό το κρασί.

possessive.rule: A genitive noun phrase or weak pronoun marks the possessor of the noun it depends on. For the article in this construction see §3.54.

subjective_objective.rule: With abstract nouns the genitive may show a looser relation. Subjective genitive: the genitive is the doer of the action in the noun; objective genitive: the genitive is what the action affects.

other_uses.el: οι Έλληνες του εικοστού πρώτου αιώνα
other_uses.en: the Greeks of the twenty-first century

depending_on_numeral_adjective_pronoun.rule: A weak pronoun in the genitive can follow a numeral, certain adjectives or pronouns to narrow the scope ('of us/you/them'). If the dependent item is a full noun phrase rather than a weak pronoun, it takes από + accusative instead (§8.2). The intensive μόνος 'alone' + genitive weak pronoun means 'by oneself' (μόνη μου, §4.9).

rules: A genitive weak pronoun may follow a comparative or relative superlative (μεγαλύτερός μου 'older than me'), but μεγαλύτερος από μένα is more usual (§10.22).
A genitive weak pronoun may depend on exclamatory words in greetings, wishes and other exclamations, showing who the wish is for (§12.3).
Some colloquial fixed expressions with a genitive noun phrase work as adverbs or adjectives.
Certain formal prepositions govern the genitive (§8.2).
A genitive may depend on an omitted noun ('John's [house]').

examples.en: I hope he gets well soon!
I didn't find a dress that was any good.

examples.el: Η κοντή φούστα είναι της μόδας.
Αυτό το σπίτι μοιάζει με του Γιάννη.

vocative.title: The use of the vocative
vocative.rule: The vocative marks the person or thing being addressed. In familiar speech it may be preceded by μωρέ, ρε or βρε (uninflected; §12.1).

definite_article_use.title: The use of the definite article
definite_article_use.rule: The definite article marks a specific item, much as in English (ο σκύλος 'the dog' vs ένας σκύλος 'a dog'). Forms: §3.6. Greek also uses it in these further cases:

extra_uses.use: proper names of specific persons and places (not in the vocative: Μαρία! Κύριε Παπαδόπουλε!)
noun + possessive: with the article = 'my' etc.; without it = 'of mine'
with the quantifiers όλος 'all' and ολόκληρος 'whole' (the latter may drop the article)
abstract nouns seen as a definite entity
plural nouns and adjectives denoting whole classes; also nouns like ποδόσφαιρο where English has no article

examples.en: Young people listen to music all the time.

extra_uses.use: days, months, years, seasons, festivals: naming the item (nominative) or, in the accusative, the occasion

examples.en: I prefer Saturday (cf. ένα Σάββατο 'one Saturday').
On Saturday we'll go for an outing.
It rains a lot in February.

examples.el: Ο περασμένος χειμώνας ήταν πολύ βαρύς.

examples.en: We went to Crete at Easter.

extra_uses.en: on the fourth [of the month]; at four (o'clock)

examples.en: one and a half million a month

extra_uses.use: neuter article turns any word or phrase into a noun phrase or noun clause: another part of speech, a word being talked about, or a complement clause (esp. before the main clause)

examples.el: Αυτός ποτέ δεν σκέφτεται το αύριο.
examples.en: He never thinks about tomorrow (αύριο is normally an adverb).

examples.el: Το ότι δεν γύρισε ακόμα είναι κακό σημάδι.
examples.en: That (s)he hasn't come back yet is a bad sign.

examples.el: Το να λες τέτοια πράγματα είναι δύσκολο.
examples.en: To say such things is difficult.

extra_uses.use: article normally repeated before each noun in a coordinated sequence when the first has one

indefinite_article_use.title: The use of the indefinite article
indefinite_article_use.rule: ένας, μια, ένα basically means 'one' and can also act as a pronoun like κάποιος 'someone'. It does not always match English 'a/an'. Forms: §3.7.

examples.en: I saw a (female) friend of yours.

absence_of_article.title: Absence of article
absence_of_article.rule: Greek often has no article where English uses 'a', 'any' or 'some'.

cases.use: object of a verb when definiteness is not stressed (fixed expressions; questions, negatives, conditionals)

examples.en: At last I've found a watch.

examples.el: Αν είχα κινητό θα τον έπαιρνα.
examples.en: If I had a mobile I would call him.
Have you any brothers and sisters?
I don't have any brothers and sisters.

cases.use: indefinite subject, esp. in questions, negatives, conditionals

examples.el: Υπάρχει γυναίκα που να μην το ξέρει;
examples.en: Is there a woman who doesn't know it?

examples.el: Δεν υπάρχει γυναίκα που να μην το ξέρει.
examples.en: There isn't a woman who doesn't know it.

examples.el: Αν με ρωτούσε γυναίκα, θα την έστελνα στη συνάδελφό μου.
examples.en: If a woman asked me, I would send her to my (female) colleague.
Some wine has spilled on the tablecloth.

adjective_use.title: The use of adjectives
adjective_use.rule: Adjectives inflect for gender, number and case (forms §3.32-3.47) and modify nouns attributively or predicatively; they agree with the noun in gender, number and case.

attributive.rule: Normally directly before the noun. After the noun it is emphatic, and if the noun has the definite article the article is repeated before the adjective.

examples.en: a black dog (as opposed to another colour)
the black cat (as opposed to cats of another colour)

predicative.rule: The adjective refers to the subject or direct object without being in the same phrase and agrees with it. It may refer to a pronoun or an unmentioned item.

adjective_use.participles: The passive perfect participle behaves like an adjective, attributively (μια παγωμένη μπίρα 'a chilled beer') and predicatively (§6.16).

nationality.rule: For nationality Greek uses a noun where English uses an adjective; adjectives are used for non-human things.

examples.el: ο Άγγλος πρωθυπουργός / η Αγγλίδα πρωθυπουργός

adjective_as_noun.rule: Adjectives can be used as nouns, also in the singular. Many specific items omit the noun (in brackets).

genitive_weak_pronoun.rule: Shows possession; γνωστός 'known' regularly takes one for the person it is known to.

examples.en: our old house (= previous house; cf. το παλιό σπίτι μας 'our house which is old')
a (female) professor who is an acquaintance of mine

complements.rule: Complements may be prepositional phrases or clauses with να or ότι.

examples.el: Είναι ικανός να κάνει αυτή τη δουλειά;
examples.en: Is he capable of doing this job?

examples.el: Δεν είναι σίγουρο ότι θα έρθουν.
